question: An engineer must configure a Cisco UCS blade system that is managed by Cisco UCS Manager. All four connected interfaces between the blade system and the fabric interconnects must be used. Additionally, the connectivity must tolerate any link failure between the I/O module and the fabric interconnects. Which action accomplishes these requirements?
options: Configure chassis/FEX discovery policy action to four links.
Configure port aggregation with LACP policy set to default.
Configure Link Group Preference to Port Channel.
Configure Firmware Auto Sync Server policy to Auto Acknowledge.
theory: To use all four links between a chassis's I/O module and the fabric interconnects as an aggregated bundle that survives an individual link failure, the chassis discovery/connectivity behavior must be set to Port Channel mode via the Link Group Preference (rather than the default discrete/pinned-links mode). Port Channel mode bundles all discovered IOM-to-FI links into a single logical channel, so traffic redistributes across the remaining links automatically if one physical link fails, whereas discrete link pinning would simply drop the server traffic pinned to a failed individual link. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Chassis/IOM Connectivity, Link Group Preference)
